transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I don't really feel safe talking here, but I had to come because I'm being watched. There are people monitoring my every move, and the anxiety is just too much to handle. I know they are tracking me.
Have you been feeling unusually sad or depressed, or on the contrary, unusually energetic and impulsive, when you're not focused on these monitoring concerns?
No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of extreme mood shifts. I don't feel unusually depressed or super energetic and impulsive. My main issue is just the constant stress of being watched.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "duration of delusions",
  "question": "How long have you been feeling that you're being monitored or watched?"
It's been going on for about a year now. It started out slowly, but now it feels like it's happening every single day.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "functional impairment",
  "question": "Has this belief that you're being monitored affected your ability to work, study, or maintain relationships?"

Yes, it has completely ruined my life. I've stopped talking to my family and friends because I just don't know who I can trust anymore. It's also made it impossible to focus on my work, so I've barely been able to do anything lately.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "mood episode timing",
  "question": "Have you ever had periods of low mood or elevated energy that lasted for days or weeks and occurred separately from your concerns about being monitored?"

No, I haven't really experienced periods of low mood or high energy like that on their own. Any distress or anxiety I have is always directly because of the constant monitoring. It's not a separate mood issue; it's just the fear of what they are doing to me.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Delusional Disorder", "Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)", "Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)"], but based on this conversation, both Schizoaffective subtypes are now unlikely because the patient has no history of independent mood episodes (depression or mania) occurring outside of the context of the delusional belief. The delusion of being monitored is persistent, lasts more than one month, and is associated with significant functional impairment. There are no features suggesting mood episodes required for schizoaffective disorder, and no symptoms of other psychotic disorders like hallucinations or disorganized thinking. Therefore, the only remaining candidate is Delusional Disorder, with a persecutory type delusion.
